facts.fact: The World Bank's results framework for the BRIDGE project counts 510 local government administration offices connected to broadband internet, at the July 2025 baseline and unchanged at 17 December 2025, against a target of 3,428 by September 2030; the figure is a count of offices and no number of local governments is given.
facts.system: Facilities connected to broadband internet (BRIDGE results indicator)

facts.fact: The World Bank's BRIDGE results framework counts local government administration offices themselves as facilities connected to broadband internet, 510 of them at 17 December 2025; it does not say who provides or pays for the connections.
facts.system: Facilities connected to broadband internet (BRIDGE results indicator)

facts.fact: The World Bank's BRIDGE results framework records 510 local government administration offices as connected to broadband internet at 17 December 2025 and names no use made of the connection.
facts.system: Facilities connected to broadband internet (BRIDGE results indicator)

facts.fact: The World Bank's BRIDGE project, approved 6 October 2025 and closing 30 September 2030, sets a target of 3,428 local government administration offices connected to broadband internet by September 2030, within 59,103 facilities, as stated in its status report of 24 July 2026.
facts.system: Building Resilient Digital Infrastructure for Growth - BRIDGE (P508383)

facts.fact: The World Bank reports the BRIDGE project financed by an IDA credit of US$500m, of which nothing was disbursed at 24 July 2026, with a target of US$1,100m of private capital of which none was mobilised; no domestic budget line is stated.
facts.system: Building Resilient Digital Infrastructure for Growth - BRIDGE (P508383)

facts.fact: The World Bank names the Federal Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy as the BRIDGE project's implementing agency, with an established implementation unit, and says a special purpose vehicle with private investors, not yet incorporated at 24 July 2026, will eventually manage the fibre deployment.
facts.system: Building Resilient Digital Infrastructure for Growth - BRIDGE (P508383)

facts.fact: The World Bank's status report of 24 July 2026 shows local government administration offices connected at 510 in both July 2025 and December 2025, no fibre added by the project against a 90,000 km target at 10 April 2026 and nothing disbursed of US$500m.
facts.system: Building Resilient Digital Infrastructure for Growth - BRIDGE (P508383)

facts.fact: The World Bank reports that the BRIDGE project was declared effective on 27 April 2026 and that selection of private investors for its special purpose vehicle began in April 2026.
facts.system: Building Resilient Digital Infrastructure for Growth - BRIDGE (P508383)

systems.system: Building Resilient Digital Infrastructure for Growth - BRIDGE (P508383)
systems.owner: Federal Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy as implementing agency; a special purpose vehicle with private investors to manage deployment
systems.tiers: 90,000 km of new fibre targeted; facilities connected to broadband to rise from 33,628 to 59,103 by September 2030, of which local government administration offices from 510 to 3,428, health facilities from 14,366 to 16,872 and public schools from 18,752 to 38,803

note: The count is of local government administration offices, with a target of 3,428 that exceeds the number of local governments, so it is not a count of local governments; the 510 are a baseline the project inherits, not its output.
